explicit_detail: Simon Peter falls at Jesus' knees and calls himself a sinful man.
sequence_boundary: This self-description is not stated in Matthew 4 or Mark 1.
speaker: Simon Peter

explicit_detail: Luke says James and John are Simon's partners and that after bringing the boats to land they left everything and followed Jesus.
sequence_boundary: Matthew/Mark present a different local sequence.
speaker: Narrator

explicit_detail: John says two of John the Baptist's disciples followed Jesus after hearing the Baptist identify him.
sequence_boundary: Do not equate this scene with the Sea of Galilee fishermen call.
speaker: John the Baptist / Narrator

explicit_detail: Andrew is identified as one of the two and tells Simon that they have found the Messiah before bringing him to Jesus.
sequence_boundary: The other of the two disciples is not named in this passage.
speaker: Narrator / Andrew

explicit_detail: Jesus finds Philip and says 'Follow me'; Philip is said to be from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
sequence_boundary: Do not import the fishing-net setting into this Johannine scene.
speaker: Jesus / Narrator

explicit_detail: Philip finds Nathanael; Nathanael questions whether anything good can come from Nazareth, and Philip invites him to come and see.
sequence_boundary: Nathanael is not part of the Matthew 4/Mark 1 fishermen-call wording.
speaker: Philip / Nathanael

explicit_detail: Matthew says Jesus came to his own city and a paralytic lying on a bed was brought to him.
sequence_boundary: Mark explicitly names Capernaum; Matthew 9:1–8 does not.
speaker: Narrator

explicit_detail: Jesus sees their faith and tells the paralytic that his sins are forgiven.
sequence_boundary: Matthew does not describe four carriers or a roof opening.
speaker: Jesus

explicit_detail: Some scribes say to themselves that Jesus is blaspheming, and Jesus addresses their thoughts.
sequence_boundary: Mark gives a fuller internal-reasoning formulation.
speaker: scribes / Jesus

explicit_detail: Matthew ends with the crowds marveling and glorifying God who had given such authority to men.
sequence_boundary: Do not replace Matthew's closing reaction with Mark's 'we never saw anything like this'.
speaker: Narrator

explicit_detail: Mark explicitly locates the scene in Capernaum after some days, with a crowd filling the house and doorway.
sequence_boundary: Matthew calls it Jesus' own city but does not narrate the crowded doorway.
speaker: Narrator

explicit_detail: Four people carry the paralytic and open the roof because they cannot get through the crowd.
sequence_boundary: Matthew does not state the number four or the roof action.
speaker: Narrator

explicit_detail: The scribes reason in their hearts that only God can forgive sins; Jesus perceives their reasoning.
sequence_boundary: Do not import Luke's named Pharisees and teachers-of-law gathering.
speaker: scribes / Jesus

explicit_detail: The healed man immediately takes up his mat and goes out before everyone; the people say they never saw anything like it.
sequence_boundary: Matthew's crowd response is worded differently.
speaker: Narrator / crowd

explicit_detail: Luke introduces Pharisees and teachers of the law from Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem sitting while Jesus teaches.
sequence_boundary: Mark names Capernaum but Luke 5:17 does not in this scene.
speaker: Narrator

explicit_detail: Men carry a paralyzed man on a bed and lower him through the roof tiles into the middle before Jesus.
sequence_boundary: Luke does not state the number of carriers here.
speaker: Narrator

explicit_detail: Jesus calls the man 'Man' and says his sins are forgiven; scribes and Pharisees question who can forgive sins but God alone.
sequence_boundary: Mark addresses the paralytic as 'Son'; preserve witness wording.
speaker: Jesus / scribes and Pharisees

explicit_detail: Luke closes with amazement, glorifying God, fear, and the statement that they had seen strange things that day.
sequence_boundary: Do not import Mark's exact closing acclamation.
speaker: Narrator / crowd

explicit_detail: John 5 describes a different healing in Jerusalem by a pool with five covered porches; it is not the Synoptic roof-paralytic scene.
sequence_boundary: Do not harmonize John 5 with Matthew 9, Mark 2, or Luke 5.
speaker: Narrator

explicit_detail: John's healed man says he has no one to put him into the pool when the water is stirred.
sequence_boundary: The Synoptic paralytic narratives do not contain this pool explanation.
speaker: healed man

explicit_detail: Jesus tells the man to arise, take up his mat, and walk; the man is immediately made well.
sequence_boundary: Similarity of mat-language does not prove identity of events.
speaker: Jesus / Narrator

explicit_detail: John foregrounds a Sabbath controversy because the healed man carries his mat on the Sabbath.
sequence_boundary: The Synoptic roof-paralytic scene in the assigned passages is not framed as a Sabbath controversy.
speaker: Narrator / opponents

explicit_detail: Matthew introduces an unnamed ruler who says his daughter has just died and asks Jesus to lay a hand on her.
sequence_boundary: Mark and Luke name the ruler Jairus and initially describe the girl as dying.
speaker: ruler

explicit_detail: The woman has had a discharge of blood for twelve years and touches the fringe of Jesus' garment.
sequence_boundary: Matthew does not narrate physicians or expense.
speaker: Narrator

explicit_detail: Jesus turns, sees the woman, and tells her to take heart because her faith has made her well.
sequence_boundary: Matthew does not include a 'Who touched me?' exchange.
speaker: Jesus

explicit_detail: At the ruler's house Matthew mentions flute players and a noisy crowd before Jesus takes the girl by the hand and she rises.
sequence_boundary: Mark and Luke include other details not stated by Matthew.
speaker: Narrator / Jesus
